intended_object: An isomorphism Ω²(M_i) ≅ M_i in the stable module category of finitely generated modules over the truncated polynomial ring R[X]/(X^n), where M_i is the cyclic module R[X]/(X^n) ⧸ (x^i) and i ≤ n. It shows that M_i has period at most 2 under the syzygy functor. Inferred from the docstring and the surrounding file.
explanation:
The definition is the composite of two isomorphisms. The general lemma `stableModuleLoopLoopCyclicModuleIso` gives Ω²(A/aA) ≅ A/aA when the right annihilator of a is bA and the right annihilator of b is aA. Here it is applied with a = x^i and b = x^(n−i) in A = R[X]/(X^n). Both annihilator conditions hold for i ≤ n. In A, x^i·c = 0 exactly when x^(n−i) divides c, and x^(n−i)·c = 0 exactly when x^i divides c. These are the two `AdjoinRoot` lemmas the definition passes in. So the definition builds exactly the isomorphism in the docstring: two steps of the projective presentation 0 → A/x^(n−i) → A → A/x^i → 0 and its mirror image.

Degenerate cases cause no trouble. When n = 0 the ring is zero and everything is trivial. When i = 0 or i = n the modules are 0 or A, both of which are zero in the stable category.

The setting is not too narrow. The truncated polynomial ring is the specific example the result is about, and the general version for any ring with such "mutual annihilator" elements already exists as `stableModuleLoopLoopCyclicModuleIso`. The requirement that R be Noetherian is needed for finitely generated modules to form a category with kernels, so that the stable module category of finitely generated modules makes sense. Commutativity of R is needed for `AdjoinRoot`. Mathlib has no stable module category, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
